author: kathleenconnaghan5
body:
## Description

Please include a summary of the changes and a link to which issue is fixed.

[https://github.com/kathleenconnaghan5/c4615f/issues/5](url)

Added a UserConversations table to the database. This has a conversationId in each, userId column would have each userId in a conversation that matches with that conversationId. Multiple users can now have a matching conversationId.

Changed the models to reflect the loss of the user1, user 2 etc columns that were added in the last PR (read receipts)

## Notes on your approach and thought process

**Please leave some notes explaining your thought process and your approach to solving this issue.**

**What additional (non-database) changes are needed to implement this feature (we want this to be high level but thorough)?**

_Backend_
- New/update for all the get, put and post requests. Need to account for the loss of user1, user2 columns in conversations table. Same for user1LastMessageIdSeen, user2LastMessageIdSeen.

- New API routes for UserConversation. Change the routes for conversations as well.

- Redux: add in new action creators, thunks dispatch, etc for UserConversation. Change existing ones that now lead no where.

_Client_
- Sidebar will need to list all chat users, not just one. Multiple names and avatars, while keeping the unread count and message preview. Unread count would only be for the singular logged on user.

- OtherUserBubble changed to account for multiple other users. Potentially different user bubble colors. Might want to add the username above each message for clarity within ActiveChat.

- lastMessageSeen functions/thunks/etc will now connect to UserConversations rather than Conversations table, but frontend these need to have functionality for multiple avatars in ActiveChat.

----------

**If our app were already deployed, what steps would we need to take to move to this new feature without disrupting service for current users?**

A.) There are merging tools that exist to help prevent issues with db changes such as this: Flyway, Liquibase. I am not familiar with any specific option, but would look into it as a possibility.

B.) Without a separate merge tool, I would probably make a copy of the original db into "version-1" and then have the new changes put into a separate db "version-2". We would take all current conversation rows and copy that data into rows of the new table that we want to make in "version-2". The copied data would be added and tested before users were switched over.

- Usually big updates are run at a time when it is highly unlikely anyone will be using the app. Using their specific timezone location data and running it at 3am.

- Give users advance notice: via email, pop-up, confirm box, etc. That way they can plan accordingly, maybe post-pone if it's massively disruptive.

------------

**In your PR description, please explain a couple different ways we could have designed the database for this feature. What are the benefits and drawbacks of each?*

**1.** 
The way I did it: remove the user1, user2 and user1LastMessageIdSeen, user2LastMessageIdSeen from the conversation table. Create a new table UserConversations that holds all conversations that exist and for each user, the conversationId, lastMessageRead, unreadMsgCount.

_Pros:_
- Connects the conversation and the multiple users with no changes to messages and user tables.
- Would work for multiple users in one conversation, since they would all have the same conversationId, they would each have the last message they saw and their own unreadMsgCount.

_Cons:_
- Full refactor needed of the code, probably inevitable regardless.

----

**2.**
We had user1 and user2 columns in conversation, we could remove each of those columns and replace it with a new column that stores the user IDs as an array of strings in the column, rather than making a new table. We would just parse the string as an array. 

_Pros:_
- Avoids making a new table, which might reduce some of the refactor needed on the rest of the code, and might mean that there would be less disruption to current users on a deployed app.

_Cons:_
- Confusing/messy to implement.
- That's not how SQL is supposed to work, not even sure it would work without causing messy bugs.

----

**3.**
Use a different database program entirely, a NoSQL db such as MongoDB, Cassandra, etc.

_Pros:_
- Better performance and scalability, more flexible to test out possible ideas.
- Works for unstructured data like PDF files, photos, videos. Which might be necessary for this application in future.

_Cons:_
- Less general and the database can get too big since NoSQL isn't designed to remove duplicated data.
- Way more work to start from scratch, foolish since we have a working db and this application is relatively small.
